text.p: Mexican financial group Banamex-Accival SA (Banacci) is expected shortly to report third quarter earnings that show it is slowly emerging from a banking crisis sparked by the peso crash, according to analysts.
A survey of four bank analysts predicted that Banacci will report third quarter earnings net of revaluation surplus of 33 centavos per share.
But analysts had largely different predictions about how well the quarter went for Banacci, Mexico's largest financial group and the owner of Banamex bank.

"This could be one of the best quarters (for the group) since the peso crash," said Alberto Sanchez, a bank analyst at Bear Stearns in New York. Sanchez predicted third quarter earnings of roughly 46 centavos per share.
Banamex has struggled against rising past-due loans piled up during Mexico's recession, but should be seeing the light at the end of the tunnel.
"Past-due loans will continue to grow, but at a slightly lower rate than in previous quarters," said Carol Milnes, an analyst at Abaco Brokerage in Mexico City.

Lower interest rates in Mexico during the quarter should have helped the bank's asset quality, although loans being restructured in UDI inflation-indexed units will hurt net interest margins, analysts said.

Banamex is expected to build reserves at a steady pace ahead of new U.S. GAAP accounting rules that come into effect at the start of 1997. Rogelio Urrutia, a bank analyst at Valores Finamex, predicted the bank would create 2.5 billion pesos in reserves in the third quarter alone.
He said reserves creation would hurt earnings.
"On the bank level, they could report a loss. On the group level, it should be a slight profit," he said, predicting third quarter earnings per share of just eight centavos for the group.
Some analysts projected third quarter reserves at about 84 percent of past-due loans, up from 75 percent at the end of the second quarter.
Sanchez said that while Banamex has not been as aggressive as rival Grupo Financiero Bancomer in building reserves, it has written off a larger percentage of bad loans than Bancomer.

Banacci reported a second quarter net profit of 745 million pesos, including revaluation of subsidiaries' assets. In 1995, the group reported a nine-months net profit of 1.916 billion pesos including revaluation.
